page: Microsoft Azure L48s_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 24 physical cores configured into 48 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, equating to an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Dedicated high-capacity local storage is a primary architectural feature, bundling 12,035 GB of direct NVMe SSD capacity. The instance contains zero GPUs and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable general compute paired with strong performance in selected cryptographic and rendering workloads. The server achieves a PassMark CPU score of 48,928.12 and an encryption score of 43,900.85, both placing in the top quartile. Geekbench scores reach 1,707.0 in single-core and 15,837.0 in multi-core routines, bolstered by strong performance in ray tracing (50,093.0) and image processing (15,139.0). In data throughput, uncached read memory bandwidth measures 163.76 GB/sec while write bandwidth sustains 70.56 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 83.97 GB/sec, and in-memory key-value operations achieve 45.6 million Redis SET operations per second.

The balance between 48 dedicated compute threads, an ample 384.0 GB RAM footprint, and over 12 TB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage establishes high resource density for I/O-intensive architectures. While standard CPU throughput lands predominantly in the median performance band, qualitative hardware efficiency is driven by the vast integrated NVMe array, which mitigates network-attached disk latency overhead. This configuration is particularly suited for high-throughput transactional and NoSQL databases, distributed file systems, search index nodes, big data caching, and large-scale data processing workloads.

It features 384.0 GB of memory alongside an extensive 12,035 GB local NVMe SSD storage deployment, with no integrated GPUs. Synthetic evaluation reveals strong ratings in PassMark encryption and ray tracing, with median marks across general single-core and multi-core computational tests. Memory throughput achieves 163.76 GB/sec in uncached block reads, supporting in-memory processing tasks such as Redis SET benchmarks at 45.6 million operations per second. The dense combination of dedicated thread scheduling, generous RAM-per-core ratio, and voluminous integrated solid-state storage makes the L48s_v3 well-suited for high-throughput relational and non-relational database installations, distributed big data nodes, and large-scale I/O-heavy indexing systems.
